key_insight: DLLM decoding wastes most parallel compute because only a small subset of tokens is decodable at each diffusion step, and attention-derived token importance reliably predicts which tokens are decodable — enabling concentrated compute where it matters.
problem_solved: Reduces the high decoding compute cost of Diffusion Large Language Models (DLLMs) by avoiding wasted work on non-decodable tokens during parallel block decoding.
method: Estimate token-wise decodability using attention-derived importance scores (fast, correlated proxy).
Dynamically allocate compute to tokens predicted as decodable (mask/prune or route activations to the small subset) while skipping or deferring others.
Iteratively update decodability predictions across diffusion steps to preserve generation quality with minimal overhead.
impact: Significantly lowers inference cost and latency for DLLMs, making them more practical to deploy at scale while maintaining generation quality — enabling efficient, real-time or cost-constrained use cases.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: standard DLLM parallel block decoding (most compute wasted) vs FOCUS selective-compute flow (compute concentrated on decodable tokens).
Heatmap overlay: token attention scores correlated with token-wise decodability across diffusion steps.
Bar/line chart: compute/time vs quality comparing baseline DLLM, FOCUS, and AR baselines (showing compute savings and retained quality).
Pipeline icon set: attention scorer → decodability selector → selective compute blocks → final output (showing low overhead decision loop).
paper_title: FOCUS: DLLMs Know How to Tame Their Compute Bound
paper_authors: Kaihua Liang, Xin Tan, An Zhong, Hong Xu, Marco Canini
